title: Advanced Averages
tagline: Year 2 — Weighted averages, overlapping groups, corrections and average speed

introduction.overview: Year 1 averages were direct: sum divided by count, joining and leaving. Year 2 extends to weighted averages of several groups, overlapping groups, wrongly read data corrected later, averages changing across innings, and average speed over unequal parts of a journey. The tool remains Sum = Average × Count, used with careful bookkeeping.
introduction.placementRelevance: Average questions are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds, and multi-step ones with overlapping or corrected data are a typical intermediate-level item.
introduction.realWorldContext: Batting averages, class marks, average fuel consumption and average temperature over several days all use these methods.

learningObjectives: Compute weighted averages of groups of different sizes
Solve overlapping groups where one item is counted twice
Correct an average after a wrongly read value
Find a missing value when the average changes
Compute average speed for equal distances, equal times and unequal parts

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Sum = Average × Count. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.

coreDefinitions: Overlap: an item belonging to two groups so that adding the group totals counts it twice.
Correction: when a wrong value x was used instead of y, the corrected sum is old sum − x + y.
Average speed for equal distances: 2xy/(x + y). For equal times: (x + y)/2.
Change in average × number of items = change in total.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: An average is a balance point. Moving one item by d changes the total by d and the average by d ÷ n. So every average-change question reduces to a difference of totals.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Always convert to totals first. Do the arithmetic on totals (add, remove, replace, correct), then divide again at the end.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Correction
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: x was used instead of y.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Change in average
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: New item = Old average + (change × new count)

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Overlap
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Overlapping item = (sum of group totals) − (total of all)

mainNarrative: For weighted averages, multiply each group average by its size, add the totals and divide by the total number. 15 boys averaging 40 and 25 girls averaging 48 have totals 600 and 1200; the combined average is 1800 ÷ 40 = 45.

For overlapping groups, add the totals of the two groups and subtract the total of all items; the difference is the item counted twice. With 9 numbers averaging 22, first five averaging 20 and last five averaging 24, the fifth is 100 + 120 − 198 = 22.

For corrections, find the change in total (new − wrong value) and divide by the count. If 25 numbers average 40 and one value 25 was misread as 52, the true total is 1000 − 27 = 973 and the average 38.92.
For innings problems, the average after one more innings is (old total + new score) ÷ (n + 1). A batsman with average 48 after 12 innings scoring 100 in the 13th has (576 + 100) ÷ 13 = 52.

For average speed over equal distances, use 2xy/(x + y). For unequal parts, find the time of each part: with 2/3 of the distance at 40 km/h and 1/3 at 60 km/h, the time per km is (2/3)/40 + (1/3)/60 = 1/45, so 45 km/h.

deepDiveAspects.title: Average of an AP
deepDiveAspects.content: For consecutive or equally spaced numbers, the average equals the middle value (or the mean of the first and last). Eight consecutive numbers with average 25.5 start at 22.

deepDiveAspects.title: Why average speed is harmonic
deepDiveAspects.content: Equal distances at different speeds take different times, so the slower speed counts for more. Hence the average is less than the simple mean.

problemVariations.exampleSnippet: First five and last five of nine

solvedExamples.title: Weighted average
solvedExamples.question: A class has 15 boys with average mark 40 and 25 girls with average mark 48. Find the average of the whole class.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Girls are more numerous, so the average is closer to 48.

solvedExamples.title: Overlapping groups
solvedExamples.question: The average of 9 numbers is 22. The average of the first five is 20 and of the last five is 24. Find the fifth number.
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: The fifth number is in both groups.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The two groups together count the fifth number twice.

solvedExamples.title: Correcting an average
solvedExamples.question: The average of 25 numbers was found to be 40. Later it was discovered that 25 had been read as 52. Find the correct average.

shortcutMethods.title: Total-first method

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Convert to totals, update the total once, divide. For corrections, change in average = change in sum ÷ n.

rulesForApplication: Overlap = sum of group totals − total.
Check the answer is within the data range.

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Add group totals, subtract the whole.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: A combined average must lie between the group averages.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Write totals in a small table; avoid mental juggling.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Average-based DI questions use the same bookkeeping.

keyTakeaways: Use harmonic mean for equal distances.
selfCheckQuestions: Can I find a missing value from averages of overlapping groups?
Can I compute average speed for unequal parts?
